parts.answer_text: The longest chord of a circle is a diameter of the circle.

parts.answer_text: An arc is a semi-circle when its ends are the ends of a diameter.

parts.answer_text: Segment of a circle is the region between an arc and chord of the circle.

parts.answer_text: A circle divides the plane, on which it lies, in three parts.

question_text: Write True or False: Give reasons for your answers.

parts.part_text: Line segment joining the centre to any point on the circle is a radius of the circle.
parts.answer_text: True. All the points on the circle are at equal distances from the centre of the circle, and this equal distance is called as radius of the circle.

parts.part_text: A circle has only finite number of equal chords.
parts.answer_text: False. There are infinite points on a circle. Therefore, we can draw infinite number of chords of given length. Hence, a circle has infinite number of equal chords.

parts.part_text: If a circle is divided into three equal arcs, each is a major arc.
parts.answer_text: False. Consider three arcs of same length as AB, BC, and CA. It can be observed that for minor arc BDC, CAB is a major arc. Therefore, AB, BC, and CA are minor arcs of the circle.

parts.part_text: A chord of a circle, which is twice as long as its radius, is a diameter of the circle.
parts.answer_text: True. Let AB be a chord which is twice as long as its radius. It can be observed that in this situation, our chord will be passing through the centre of the circle. Therefore, it will be the diameter of the circle.

parts.part_text: Sector is the region between the chord and its corresponding arc.
parts.answer_text: False. Sector is the region between an arc and two radii joining the centre to the end points of the arc.

parts.part_text: A circle is a plane figure.
parts.answer_text: True. A circle is a two-dimensional figure and it can also be referred to as a plane figure.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of circle properties and definitions.

question_text: If two equal chords of a circle intersect within the circle, prove that the segments of one chord are equal to corresponding segments of the other chord.

question_image.description: Diagram illustrating the intersection of two equal chords PQ and RS within a circle.

answer_text: Let PQ and RS be two equal chords of a given circle and they are intersecting each other at point T. Draw perpendiculars OV and OU on these chords. In ∆OVT and ∆OUT, OV = OU (Equal chords of a circle are equidistant from the centre), OVT = OUT (Each 90°), OT = OT (Common). Therefore, ∆OVT ≅ ∆OUT (RHS congruence rule) implies VT = UT (By CPCT). Hence, the segments of one chord are equal to corresponding segments of the other chord.

steps.description: Identify the equal chords PQ and RS intersecting at point T.
Draw perpendiculars from the center O to the chords, creating triangles OVT and OUT.
Apply the RHS congruence rule to conclude that the segments VT and UT are equal.

final_answer: Thus, the segments of one chord are equal to the corresponding segments of the other chord.
